heading: Random labels add modest training time, with convergence slowing as corruption increases
definition: fitting random labels takes only a small constant factor more training time than fitting the true labels; convergence slows as the fraction of corrupted labels grows.
summary: Several independent studies find that convergence slows as label corruption increases, but whether the added training time is small remains disputed. Some runs fail to fit the labels, and similar Llama fine-tuning loss curves do not show how much longer fitting takes when training conditions are matched.

suggested_status.by_scale: Size-unspecified vision settings: C for unrestricted V2, with supporting results under other procedures. 1–10B: R2 for comparable fine-tuning loss curves only; the corruption-fraction clause remains untested. Toy and <1B results are not separately bucketed in the counts, so a full-V2 scale status is unclear. 10–100B and >100B: ?.
suggested_status.reason: The unrestricted claim encounters an explicit fitting failure in arXiv:2112.08798#R4 and loss-dependent scope limits in arXiv:2102.08817#R18. Supporting evidence includes comparable Llama fine-tuning curves in arXiv:2406.17642#R1, which establish loss-curve similarity rather than a matched time-to-fit factor. counts: versions.V2.verdicts.supports.studies=22, versions.V2.verdicts.limits_scope.studies=4 and versions.V2.verdicts.challenges.studies=1; these counts include record aliases and are not independent-replication totals. Scale coverage follows versions.V2.studies_by_size and versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.training.by_size.
suggested_status.open_questions: Matched clean/random wall-clock comparisons to a common fitting criterion, corruption sweeps in LLM fine-tuning, and controlled schedule, augmentation and loss comparisons would distinguish a conditional timing regularity from unrestricted easy optimization. Alias reconciliation and missing timing rows would strengthen the evidence accounting.

source.title: Understanding deep learning requires rethinking generalization
source.authors: Chiyuan Zhang; Samy Bengio; Moritz Hardt; B. Recht; O. Vinyals

original_result.setup: Zhang et al. compared convergence times for Inception, Alexnet and MLP 1x512 on CIFAR10.
original_result.result: Relative convergence-time curves covered label-corruption fractions from 0 to 1. The available evidence provides no numerical time ratios.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: A time-delay network (E-TDNN) converged faster on clean labels and learned mislabeled examples later.
Modular-addition MLP runs reached the training-accuracy threshold later as label corruption increased.
Two-layer linear networks converged equally fast on original and shuffled labels after whitening.
ImageNet learning slowed as label noise increased.
ResNet18 training loss decreased more slowly as CIFAR10 label corruption increased.
ResNet-101 needed more epochs to fit skin-lesion examples as label corruption increased.
Training took longer with corrupted labels than with clean labels.
MNIST training took longer to reach a given accuracy as label noise increased.
ImageNet learning slowed with increasing label noise across tested architectures.
MNIST networks reached minimum training loss later as label corruption increased.
With cross-entropy loss and its CE-fix variant, fitting time grew approximately linearly with label corruption.
Segmentation performance on separate evaluation data converged more slowly as more labels were randomized.
Two-layer linear networks converged more slowly with shuffled labels on natural images.
Code2Vec training trajectories changed little with noisy labels across three method-name prediction datasets.
Tested models using categorical cross-entropy or mean squared error needed few extra epochs at higher corruption.
VGG-11 took longer to fit CIFAR-10 as corruption increased when fitting succeeded.
CNNs trained with stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics needed more epochs to fit corrupted MNIST labels.
Without data augmentation, ResNet18 fit random CIFAR10 labels with no significant slowdown.
Llama 3 fine-tuning loss curves changed little between real and randomized answers.
ResNet18 trained more slowly early on as CIFAR-10 label corruption increased.
Random-label CNN training required approximately 1.6–3.1 times as many presentations to reach 95% accuracy.
MNIST MLP interpolation under UI corruption required roughly 6–7 times the clean-label epochs.
Whitening (decorrelating input features) eliminated the shuffled-label convergence slowdown in two-layer linear networks.
Supervised contrastive loss: fitting time grew faster than linearly; fully corrupted CIFAR10 exceeded available training time.
Decorrelating input features (ZCA whitening) removed the convergence-rate difference between original and shuffled labels.
Augmented random-label training slowed significantly, with roughly 3000 epochs of initial stagnation.
Completely random CIFAR-10 labels failed to fit under multi-step learning-rate decay.

untested.what: Matched wall-clock time to zero training error across both corruption fractions and dataset or model sizes.
untested.basis: arXiv:2610.16090#R4 measures presentations to 95% accuracy; its separate ensemble runtime comparison is not explicitly time to zero error. arXiv:2611.04199#R4 supplies interpolation epochs, and arXiv:2406.17642#R1 supplies loss curves rather than measured wall-clock convergence. counts: versions.V2.coverage_by_operation contains training and measurement but no scaling operation.

wording_issues.issue: The statement supplies no numerical meaning for small. For the MNIST MLP with momentum SGD and UI corruption, median interpolation epochs were 18 for clean runs and 113–122 for noisy runs, approximately 6.3–6.8 times the clean epoch count. All SGD runs interpolated at tested rates ρ=0,0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8,1. Separately, augmented random-label training includes roughly 3000 epochs of initial stagnation. These are different conditions and do not determine a common factor.

The records use presentations to 95% accuracy, total ensemble execution minutes including evaluation, iterations to zero error, and loss curves through a fixed epoch budget. The ensemble execution times are not identified as training times to a common attained fitting threshold and do not independently establish V2. These endpoints and units do not establish interchangeable timing ratios.

wording_issues.phrase: convergence slows as the fraction of corrupted labels grows
wording_issues.issue: Whitened linear networks have identical convergence rates for original and shuffled labels. Separately, Code2Vec curves are mostly nearly identical across noisy conditions. Neither establishes progressive slowing across intermediate fractions in those settings.

The numerical MLP epoch comparison uses UI class-conditional corruption; its verdict explicitly leaves timing for fully independent random labels untested. The modest-extra-epoch loss-comparison results stop at η=0.6.

Fitting fails within the tested procedure for all-random-label VGG-11 with multi-step decay. ResNet-18 supervised contrastive training on CIFAR10 does not attain exact zero training error above 80% corruption within 100k iterations. Residual training error is unreported, leaving near-zero fitting unresolved in the supervised contrastive condition.

method_sensitivity.what: ResNet18/CIFAR10 shows little random-label fitting slowdown without augmentation, but substantially increased training time with augmentation. Both V2 findings are supplied by verdict reasons and missing-row declarations.
Shuffled labels slow convergence on natural cats-and-dogs images, whereas ZCA whitening makes original-label and shuffled-label convergence rates identical in two-layer linear networks.

With ResNet-18 on CIFAR10/CIFAR100, CE and CE-fix have approximately linear corruption-dependent growth in iterations to zero training error, while supervised contrastive loss has superlinear growth. On CIFAR10 above 80% corruption, supervised contrastive loss does not attain exact zero training error within 100k iterations. Residual training error is unreported, so near-zero fitting cannot be determined.

The VGG-11 all-random-label fitting failure is associated with multi-step decay rather than the cosine-annealing procedure. The record explicitly qualifies memorization capability by training procedure.

method_sensitivity.factor: Dataset size and joint optimization policy
method_sensitivity.what: CIFAR-10 CNN memorization efficiency changes with dataset size and the joint batch-size/learning-rate policy. The reported random-to-true presentation factors belong specifically to the fixed-policy condition and the 95% accuracy threshold.

DenseNet121 random-label CIFAR10 training has slower accuracy growth, but the initial learning rate is lowered to 0.001 for that condition. The corrected row is cannot_determine for V2; the comparison does not isolate label corruption or establish a time-to-fit factor.

The MNIST MLP record contrasts a main constant-learning-rate Adam protocol that does not interpolate corrupted runs with a momentum-SGD extension using UI corruption that reaches interpolation. SGD was tested at rho=0,0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8,1, including the clean condition. All SGD runs interpolated; median interpolation epochs were 18 for clean runs and 113–122 for noisy runs, approximately 6.3–6.8 times the clean epoch count. This matched comparison belongs to the SGD extension.
